title: View spec, view/0
description: A view described once, in catalog names. It carries no sizes and no breakpoints; the container it lands in decides presentation.

title.description: Shown by the container's frame, not drawn in the scene.

use.description: A preset name. Expands into layers. Ignored if layers is present. The library ships: line, bar-list, share-bar, bar, grouped-bar, stacked-bar, stacked-area, pie, donut, pie-semi-circle, gauge, rose, radial-bar, sunburst, heatmap, funnel, box-plot, error-bars, waterfall, candlestick, fan, dumbbell, bullet, waffle, unit-chart, isotype, parliament, icon-array. Most take a dimension in query.by, and gauge and icon-array take none: resolve() says which a preset needs. A custom mark's package registers the presets that draw it, in code, with registerPreset(): the geo package registers choropleth and symbol-map, and for tiles, which are the same mark registered again with other shapes under a name the page gives, the presets the page names: tile-grid-map and hex-tile-map where the fixtures are loaded; the flow package registers sankey, and the partition package registers treemap and pair-list. A code base may also hand resolve() a library of its own. So this is not an enum: resolve() checks the name against the library and then the registry, and its error lists the presets there are.

keep.description: Parts a container may not drop.

allOf.description: A dimension needs something to draw it with: layers, or a preset.

metrics.description: Catalog metric names. The first is the primary metric.

by.description: Zero, one or two catalog dimensions. With two, a layer must encode each: the second usually goes to color, to detail, or to the other axis of a grid of cells.

field.description: A dimension name, a metric name, a companion the result returns with one, written "<metric>@<suffix>", or a number (for a rule, on x or on y).

anyOf.description: "unit" draws a value as counted glyphs, one for so many, and what one is worth is worked out from the data. Its form is what is on its channels: a dimension on x and a metric on y is a stack up from the axis; a dimension on y and a metric on x is a run along each row; a metric on x and a dimension on color is a grid of a hundred divided by share; a metric on x alone, with no dimension in the query, is that grid filled to the metric's place in its catalog domain; a metric on angle and a dimension on color, with sweep "half", is seats round a half circle. It takes no x2 or y2, no series and no negative value.

The name of a custom mark registered in code. "geo" is the one so far: one layer alone, with the dimension of region keys on x and a metric on color (a fill) or on size (a symbol). The same mark may be registered again under another name with other shapes, as "geo-tiles" and "geo-hexes" are for tile maps, and takes the same encodings. "link" is another: one layer alone, with the source dimension on x, the target dimension on y and a metric on size. A schema cannot list those: resolve() checks the name against the registry, and its error lists the marks there are.

color.description: A dimension splits the layer into series, a colour each. A metric, on a cell, on a dot in a grid or on a custom mark that reads it, is quantized to a colour ramp: the sequential one, or the diverging one where its values or its catalog domain cross zero. No field chooses the ramp.

detail.description: One of the query's dimensions. It splits the layer into a series for each value, as a dimension on color does, and paints none apart: every series is in the layer's own paint, there is no legend, and the limit of six series does not apply. Many lines in one paint. Not with the same layer's color in a plot, and not with stack. On an arc split by color it is the second ring: each segment divided among this dimension's values, in the segment's colour.

angle.description: For an arc. A metric, with a dimension on color: each segment is its share of the total, and a second dimension on detail divides each segment again in a ring outside it. A metric, with a dimension on radius: each ring's arc sweeps to its value. A metric alone is read against its catalog domain. A dimension, with a metric on radius: an equal slice for each value, in the engine's order.

radius.description: For an arc. A number is the inner radius, as a share of the outer: 0.6 makes a donut. A metric, with a dimension on angle, is how far each slice reaches from the centre, on a square-root scale, so its area carries the value: there is no inner radius then. A dimension, with a metric on angle, gives each value a ring, six at most; with nothing on angle it is the whole ring.

size.description: A metric. A dot's size is one of a few steps, and the painter says how big each is. On a dot in a grid, with a dimension on both x and y, the step is by how far the value is from zero.

x2.description: For a bar, a rule or an area with a field on x: its second end. The mark runs from the value on x to this one.

y2.description: For a bar, a rule or an area with a field on y: its second end. The mark runs from the value on y to this one.

series.description: "previous" draws the comparison companion of the metric. On a text layer in rows, "delta" says each row's change on the previous period, painted by the metric's polarity. Either needs "compare" in the query.

stack.description: On a layer split by color: each series starts where the one under it ends. "normalize" makes each a share of the whole, and "center" sets each stack half on either side of zero. A bar split by color with no stack sits beside its neighbours. A unit takes none, but "normalize" on its grid, which is shares already.

sweep.description: On an arc: the arcs run over the top half of the circle and not all the way round. For a circle divided by color and for a gauge; not with a dimension on angle or on radius. On a unit with a metric on angle: its seats sit round that half, and it is required. The one layer field that is neither data nor role.

paint.description: A paint token, never a colour: series.1 to series.6, compare, rule, ink, ink.muted, delta. A layer with none takes series.1, so a second metric on the same plot wants "series.2". "delta" is the paint of the metric's change over the range: good or bad by its polarity, and the layer's own where there is no change to judge.
